summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA assesses T-Mobile as the third and final stock in his series on SpaceX's threat to US telecoms, having already covered Verizon and AT&T. SpaceX is expanding its ambitions, and the three incumbents face disruption from a rival that raised roughly $100 billion in its recent IPO at a nearly $2 trillion valuation, with Elon Musk able to raise capital cheaply from loyal investors despite SpaceX being loss-making. T-Mobile is the fastest-growing of the three: earnings per share are expected to grow nearly 18% over the next several years, versus about 10% for AT&T and 8% for Verizon, revenue grew nearly double digits last quarter, and management forecasts nearly 1 million net additions in 2026. Its operating margin has almost tripled over a decade, from roughly 7% in 2017 to 21.8% trailing, and at about $114 billion of long-term debt it is less indebted than its rivals — though all three carry heavy debt that leaves little room to retaliate against SpaceX. The valuation has fallen to its lowest forward P/E in years, below its long-term EPS growth rate, a PEG under one. His discounted cash flow model gives a fair value of $222 against a current price of $159. Call: TMUS BUY reiterated, conviction upgraded from low to medium on 4 November 2026.
